newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate approves chemical weapons treaty.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate approves chemical weapons treaty.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday approved an international treaty outlawing chemical weapons, handing President Bill Clinton a foreign policy victory.
The vote was 74-26 -- seven more than the two-thirds majority needed for consenting to ratification of the Chemical Weapons Convention, already ratified by 74 countries.

It came after the Senate had stripped out a series of "killer" amendments that would have set insuperable conditions on U.S. ratification. Twenty-eight other understandings and clarifications agreed to by the administration were attached to the resolution of ratification.

The treaty's fate had appeared to be in doubt a week ago, but intensive negotiations between key senators and administration officials met many concerns and finally persuaded Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott to break with fellow conservatives and support the treaty.
The treaty, which comes into effect next Tuesday, aims to ban the production, stockpiling, transfer and use of chemical weapons worldwide.
